program_meta.program_name: MSc Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Science and Engineering (FSE), taught within the Bernoulli Institute for Mathematics, Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence. Five specializations: Machine Learning, Hybrid Intelligence, Robotics, Multi-Agent Systems, AI Engineering; also a non-technical 'Science, Business and Policy' track. Croho code 66981. 24 months, 120 EC.
program_meta.degree_target: MSc (this is a taught Master's, not a PhD position; PhD entry in the Netherlands is normally via a separate paid PhD vacancy, not a doctoral application cycle)
program_meta.sop_limit: NOT a conventional SOP/essay. Verbatim from the Registration Procedure: applicants complete a checklist requiring them to 'By answering the questions in the Motivation table, explain why you choose to apply for this Master's degree programme.' No word/page limit stated anywhere for this Motivation table; treat as 'not stated'.
program_meta.extra_essays: The registration checklist (docx: https://www.rug.nl/fse/education/admission-application/apply-msc/nl-diploma/ai-checklist.docx) requires, verbatim: '(1) Provide at least one reference letter and/or contact (name and research institute) we may approach for a reference. (2) By answering the questions in the Motivation table, explain why you choose to apply for this Master's degree programme. (3) Describe your pre-education. (4) Provide a bachelor thesis or another individually written report in English of an academic assignment. If you have not completed such a report, an assignment will be given to you by the Board of Admissions. (5) Curriculum Vitae.' Note item (4): a written academic report/thesis sample is mandatory, functionally replacing a research statement.
program_meta.deadline_fall_2027: 01 May 2027 for Dutch, EU/EEA, and non-EU/EEA students alike, for a 1 September 2027 start (verbatim table on the programme page). EARLY-DECISION MECHANISM (verbatim): 'Do not wait until 1 May, but use one of the earlier deadlines... Application – Decision: 1 December – 15 January / 1 February – 1 March / 15 March – 15 April / 1 May – 15 June.' Given a Fall 2027 target, submitting by 1 December 2026 or 1 February 2027 secures a decision months earlier and is recommended.
program_meta.lor_count: At least ONE. Verbatim: 'Provide at least one reference letter and/or contact (name and research institute) we may approach for a reference.' Note this explicitly allows naming a referee contact in lieu of a submitted letter, which is unusually flexible versus most programs on this list.

program_meta.advisor_model: NOT a PhD-style advisor-admission model - this is a taught MSc. Admission is via a programme-level Board of Admissions ('The Board of Admissions will decide whether you can be admitted to the Master's degree programme'), not a named faculty advisor. Individual faculty become relevant only at the MSc thesis stage (typically final semester/year), where students choose a supervisor from among Bernoulli Institute staff teaching in the programme, per the page's own framing: 'Most of the teachers in the Master's programme also participate as researchers in the research institute Bernoulli. The content of the courses taught are closely linked to the research themes of the teachers.'
program_meta.ms_research_access: Yes, structurally built in. Programme page states, verbatim: 'Challenging graduation projects: as the distance between students and teachers is small, you will work on real-life scientific problems during your studies.' MSc thesis work is done within Bernoulli Institute research groups; several alumni testimonials describe thesis projects done in collaboration with external partners (e.g., TNO) as well as with RUG groups. No formal 'rotation' system found; thesis-lab matching appears informal/direct-contact based, typical of Dutch technical MSc programmes.
program_meta.notes: STRUCTURAL RED FLAG FOR THIS APPLICANT'S STATED GOAL: Akshat's brief specifies 'MS->PhD track in Europe'; Groningen's AI Master is a standard 2-year taught MSc with a thesis, not a PhD-track or MSc-then-automatic-PhD pipeline. Progression to a Groningen PhD after this MSc would require a SEPARATE, competitive application to a funded PhD vacancy (a paid RUG staff position, not an academic admission), same as at any other Dutch university - there is no guaranteed or fast-tracked MS->PhD bridge described anywhere in the sourced pages. Tuition (2026-2027 rates, non-EU/EEA): EUR 24,900/year; EU/EEA: EUR 2,694/year - a real cost factor since Akshat is a non-EU/EEA (Indian) applicant. NL Scholarship (EUR 5,000, one-time) and ASML Scholarship (EUR 5,000/year, competitive, 40 slots university-wide) are the two named funding mechanisms; neither covers full non-EU tuition. Admission requirements table names required prior coursework verbatim: 'Calculus, Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics, Advanced Programming, Machine Learning, Advanced Logic, Neural Networks, Research Methodology Skills' - Akshat's CSE-with-AI-specialization B.Tech should cover most of these, but 'Advanced Logic' is a possible gap worth checking against his actual transcript before applying.

faculty.department: Artificial Intelligence — Bernoulli Institute, Faculty of Science and Engineering
faculty.lab: Not separately named; personal group page (mvaldenegro.github.io) is a stale/placeholder template with dummy 'Paper Title Number N' entries and 'Recent Publications: Upcoming!' - use DBLP for real output, not his own site.
faculty.research_areas: Uncertainty quantification in deep neural networks (aleatoric/epistemic disentanglement, Bayesian neural networks, ensembles), explainability and saliency-map reliability, out-of-distribution detection, applications to robot vision, underwater/sonar perception, biosignals, and medical/generative models.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's semi-supervised spine-MRI work used MC-dropout uncertainty combined with confidence thresholding to filter pseudo-labels, and found that per-class thresholds calibrated on 5 reference images match those from 304 - a direct empirical statement about how much epistemic-uncertainty signal is actually needed to make a filtering decision reliable. Valdenegro-Toro's 'A Deeper Look into Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty Disentanglement' (CVPR Workshops 2022) and 'Can Bayesian Neural Networks Explicitly Model Input Uncertainty?' (VISAPP 2025) are the exact methodological machinery Akshat used informally; his 'Disentangled Uncertainty and Out of Distribution Detection in Medical Generative Models' (arXiv 2022) is a direct precedent for Akshat's A-PDF post-hoc plausibility filter on cWGAN-GP-generated pseudo-images, since both are about catching bad generative-model output using uncertainty/OOD signal rather than trusting the generator.
faculty.key_paper_1: A Deeper Look into Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty Disentanglement. CVPR Workshops, 2022.
faculty.key_paper_2: Can Bayesian Neural Networks Explicitly Model Input Uncertainty? VISAPP (VISIGRAPP), 2025. (See also: Disentangled Uncertainty and Out of Distribution Detection in Medical Generative Models, arXiv:2211.06250, 2022; Sub-Ensembles for Fast Uncertainty Estimation in Neural Networks, ICCV Workshops, 2023.)

faculty.rank: Full Professor, Machine Learning: Theory and Applications
faculty.department: Bernoulli Institute for Mathematics, Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science Department, Intelligent Systems Group. Also Honorary Professor of Machine Learning, University of Birmingham (Center for Systems Modelling and Quantitative Biomedicine).
faculty.lab: Not separately named; personal group page at cs.rug.nl/~biehl
faculty.research_areas: Theory and algorithm development for neural networks and machine learning; Learning Vector Quantization and Relevance Learning; statistical physics of learning (dynamics of ML processes, disordered systems); applications in life sciences, biomedical data (EMG, FDG PET neuroimaging), and astroinformatics.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's cross-cutting empirical puzzle - a diffusion encoder that transfers well for liver segmentation but fails below random initialization for kidney - is fundamentally a question about what a learned representation captures and why it generalizes selectively. Biehl's ongoing 2026 work, 'Autoencoders versus PCA for feature extraction in FDG PET scans in neurodegenerative diseases' (ESANN 2026) and 'Aligning generalization between humans and machines' (Nature Machine Intelligence, 2026), both interrogate what a learned feature-extraction method actually captures versus a simpler baseline, in medical-imaging and biosignal settings closely analogous to Akshat's abdominal-CT work. His long-standing Learning Vector Quantization / Relevance Learning line is also a natural fit for Akshat's honors-thesis interest in interpretable per-class thresholding.
faculty.key_paper_1: Aligning generalization between humans and machines. Nature Machine Intelligence, 2026.
faculty.key_paper_2: Autoencoders versus PCA for feature extraction in FDG PET scans in neurodegenerative diseases. ESANN, 2026. (See also: FA(IR)^2MA-GMLVQ - A hidden-feature-bias mitigation approach for fairness in classification learning based on generalized matrix learning vector quantization, Neurocomputing, 2026.)
faculty.taking_students: Ambiguous/discouraging signal. No explicit 'yes' statement, but the site is clearly active (news updated through August 2026, ongoing co-authored papers with named PhD-level collaborators). Directly contradicted by his own contact-policy statement below.

faculty.email_angle: Do not cold-email per his own explicit instruction; if a formally announced vacancy or MSc-thesis slot appears, the angle would be: your work on aligning generalization between human and machine representations is the theory I need to explain why my frozen diffusion encoder transferred anatomical structure for liver but not kidney.
faculty.notes: RED FLAG, explicit and decisive: he states unsolicited applications 'will probably remain unanswered' - this is the strongest do-not-cold-email signal found across any faculty member on this list. Useful to name in the Motivation table as evidence of institute depth in ML theory + biomedical applications, not as a primary contact target.
